newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu slips vs dlr as leu squeeze eases.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu slips vs dlr as leu squeeze eases.

text.p: Romania's leu ended Thursday lower at about 6,900/7,000 to the dollar against 6,100/300 at open as pressure on the money market eased amid fresh leu inflows and with central bank offering more refinancing funds.
"As banks managed to lure depositors with higher rates, the leu shortages narrowed and one-week money market rates fell to some 446 percent from 500," said a trader with a local bank.
Commercial banks' deposit rates surged to some 150 percent from 40 percent earlier this year after the BNR drive to mop up liquidity from the market to combat rising inflation.
The BNR's tighter monetary policy pushed the auctioned credit rate to an all-time high of 426.5 percent last week from about 53 percent earlier in New Year.
"The leu's rally against the dollar faded away as the greenback took advantage of the central bank's (BNR) step to inject more funds today," said another dealer.
The BNR on Thursday raised its refinancing funds on offer to 660 billion lei from 510 billion, while keeping the minimum permitted rate flat at 226 percent.
Dealers expected the dollar to consolidate at about 7,000/500 lei in the coming days with more leu funds seen flowing into the market.
"Some banks renounced to extend the rollover T-bills and this might send money market rates to about 350/380 percent in the next few days," said one trader.
Latest central bank data put interbank volume at $8.47 million on Wednesday, with overall trading at $24.75 million.
Leu-dollar retail rates ranged from 6,500/7,500 to 7,000/8,000.
